A block of mass 5 kg is put on top of piston and allowed to attain the equilibrium as in figure (b). The temperature of gas becomes $T_1$. After removing the block piston moves upward and when equilibrium is attained again temperature of gas becomes $T_2$. Neglect atmospheric pressure.
\bfig{213.9}{SII09_p2_phy_s2_q05_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$T_1=\dfrac53T_0$}
\opt{B}{$T_1=\dfrac73T_0$}
\opt{C}{$T_2=\dfrac54T_0$}
\opt{D}{$T_2=\dfrac74T_0$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\opt{D}{$v_6<v_7$ and $U_6<U_7$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SII46-P1-PHY-S2-Q04, source={Score-II - Test 46 (26 Mar 2025)}, paper=1, qno=4, type=numerical, subtopic={Kinetic theory}, answer={Bonus}, answer_src=solved, working={Printed key omits the numerical-section answers for this subject and the question was not solved; banked as Bonus.}, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: standard problem in this chapter, kinetic theory, apply the relevant results | steps: apply the relevant results; compute}]
Atoms of type A fly along the axis of a cylindrical pipe of radius R and collide with practically motionless atoms of type B. The kinetic energy of atoms A is equal to the threshold energy, so that a central impact forms a molecule AB, which then moves with velocity v. In the case of an off-centre impact, the reaction does not occur, i.e. the atoms collide elastically. In what minimum time (in sec) after the collision will atoms of type B be able to get from the axis of the cylinder to the wall of the cylinder? (R = 10 cm and v = 40 cm/s)
\end{bankq}

\begin{bankq}[id=SA30-P2-PHY-S3-Q05, source={Score Advanced - Test 30 (04 May 2024)}, paper=2, qno=5, type=numerical, subtopic={Gas laws}, answer={2}, answer_src=key, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S1 I2 C2 F1}, diff_note={concepts: standard problem in this chapter, gas laws, apply the relevant results | steps: apply the relevant results; compute}, also_in={Score Advanced - Test 31 (04 May 2024) P2 Q5}]
Troposphere is the lowest layer of atmosphere, whose temperature decreases linearly with height (y) according to T = T$_0$ $-$ $\alpha$y, where T$_0$ is temperature at Earth's surface and the constant $\alpha$ is called lapse rate of temperature. The average molar mass of normal atmospheric air is M$_0$ kg/mole and for the height of troposphere, the gravity field g is constant. The atmospheric pressure at ground is P$_0$ and gas constant is R.\par
The atmospheric pressure as a function of height y will be P (y) = P$_0\left(1-\dfrac{\alpha\mathrm y}{\mathrm T_0}\right)^{\frac{\mathrm{nM}_0\mathrm g}{2\alpha\mathrm R}}$, then value of n is :-
\end{bankq}
